{{Short description|7th-century astronomer}}
'''Abiyun al-Bitriq''' ({{langx|ar|ابيون البطريق}}, {{Transliteration|ar|DIN|''abiyūn al-biṭrīq''}}, [[floruit|fl.]] 630 CE<ref name="Bladel"/>) was a mathematician and a maker of astronomical instruments at the beginnings of Islam.<ref name="GAS">{{harvnb|Sezgin|1978}}</ref> He is mentioned in [[al-Qifti]]'s ''Tarikh al-Hukama'' as Anibun ({{lang|ar|أنبون}}, {{Transliteration|ar|DIN|''anibūn''}}),{{efn|Ta'rīḫ al-Ḥukamā', {{lang|ar|أنبون}} page ٧١ (71) in Lippert's edition ({{harvnb|Lippert|1903}})<ref name="GAS"/>}} and [[Ibn al-Nadim|al-Nadim's]]  ''Fihrist''.{{efn|Kitāb al-Fihrist, {{lang|ar|ابيون البطريق}} page ٢٧٠ (270) in Flügel's edition ({{harvnb|Flügel|1871}})<ref name="GAS"/>}}<ref name="Bladel">{{harvnb|Bladel|2008}}</ref> His name is not certain,<ref name="GAS"/> and it was probably ''Apion'' ({{langx|grc|Ἀπίων}})<ref>{{harvnb|Flügel|1871|p=24}}</ref> or ''Apion [[Patrikios]]'' ({{langx|grc|Ἀπίων Πατρίκιος}}).<ref name="Bladel"/> He wrote a book, now lost, titled "''On Operating the Planispherical Astrolabe''" ({{langx|ar|كتاب العمل بالاسطرلاب المسطح}}, {{Transliteration|ar|DIN|''kitāb al-ʿamal bi-l-asṭurlāb al-musaṭṭaḥ''}})<ref name="Bladel"/><ref name="GAS"/>
